texts.title: The Art of War
texts.author: Sun Tzu
texts.description: The classic treatise on strategy, conflict, and leadership. Thirteen chapters on planning, maneuver, terrain, and the use of spies, framed as the disciplined avoidance of needless battle.

texts.title: Tao Te Ching
texts.author: Lao Tzu
texts.description: The foundational text of Daoism. Eighty-one brief chapters on the Way (Tao), effortless action (wu wei), and the quiet power of yielding, softness, and simplicity.

texts.title: Meditations
texts.author: Marcus Aurelius
texts.description: The private Stoic notebook of a Roman emperor. Twelve books of aphoristic reflections on duty, mortality, the discipline of perception, and living in accord with nature.

texts.title: The Analects of Confucius
texts.author: Confucius
texts.description: Sayings and conversations of Confucius recorded by his disciples. Twenty books on virtue, ritual, learning, and the conduct of the good ruler and the cultivated person.

texts.title: The Enchiridion
texts.author: Epictetus
texts.description: A compact Stoic handbook compiled by Arrian from the teachings of Epictetus. Fifty-two short chapters on what is and isn't in our control, and the discipline of desire and judgment.

texts.title: The Prince
texts.author: Niccolò Machiavelli
texts.description: A blunt Renaissance manual on acquiring and holding political power. Twenty-six chapters on principalities, arms, fortune, and the gap between how rulers ought to act and how they must.

texts.title: The Bhagavad Gita
texts.author: Vyasa (traditional)
texts.description: A dialogue on the eve of battle between the warrior Arjuna and Krishna, rendered in verse as 'The Song Celestial.' Eighteen chapters on duty, devotion, and detached action.

texts.title: The Nicomachean Ethics
texts.author: Aristotle
texts.description: Aristotle's inquiry into the good life and human flourishing (eudaimonia). Ten books on virtue as a mean, friendship, pleasure, justice, and the activity of contemplation.

texts.title: Thus Spake Zarathustra
texts.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
texts.description: Nietzsche's philosophical novel in the voice of a prophet descending from the mountains. Speeches and parables on the Übermensch, eternal recurrence, and the revaluation of values.

texts.title: The Quran
texts.author: Traditional (revealed text)
texts.description: The central scripture of Islam, presented in canonical surah order 1-114. Rodwell's 19th-century English translation of the recited revelation.

texts.title: The Torah (Five Books of Moses)
texts.author: Traditional
texts.description: The first five books of the Hebrew Bible — Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy — in the JPS 1917 translation. Narrative, law, and covenant.

texts.title: Principal Upanishads
texts.author: Anonymous (ancient Hindu sages)
texts.translator: Swami Paramananda (Isa, Katha, Kena, 1919); Robert Ernest Hume (remaining 8, 1921)
texts.description: Foundational Vedantic texts on the self (Atman), ultimate reality (Brahman), and their identity. Covers eleven principal Upanishads: Isa, Katha, and Kena (Paramananda, with commentary) plus Mundaka, Prasna, Mandukya, Aitareya, Taittiriya, Brihadaranyaka, Chandogya, and Svetashvatara (Hume).
texts.notes: Units 34-163 use Hume's 1921 translation from archive.org OCR (units 1-33 are Paramananda 1919). The Hume OCR is rough — Brihadaranyaka (units 77-116) and Chandogya (units 117-151), the two longest, in particular warrant a hand-cleanup pass. Maitri and Kaushitaki, present in Hume, are not included.

texts.title: The Bible (World English Bible)
texts.author: Traditional
texts.description: The complete Protestant canon (66 books) in the World English Bible, a modern public-domain translation based on the ASV 1901. Medium-tier groupings map one unit per book.

texts.title: Confessions
texts.author: Saint Augustine of Hippo
texts.description: Augustine's spiritual autobiography and the first great Western confessional work. Thirteen books tracing his restless path from sin to conversion and into meditation on memory, time, and God.

texts.title: The Dhammapada
texts.author: Anonymous (Buddhist canon)
texts.description: A collection of the Buddha's sayings in verse, among the most widely read Buddhist scriptures. Short chapters on the mind, craving, the self, and the path to peace.

texts.title: The Great Learning and The Doctrine of the Mean
texts.author: Confucius (attributed to Zengzi and Zisi)
texts.description: Two short Confucian classics. The Great Learning lays out self-cultivation as the root of ordered society; the Doctrine of the Mean explores sincerity, balance, and the Way of the noble person.

texts.title: The Imitation of Christ
texts.author: Thomas à Kempis
texts.description: A medieval devotional classic on humility, interior life, and following Christ. Four books of brief, meditative counsels written for spiritual self-examination.

texts.title: On Liberty
texts.author: John Stuart Mill
texts.description: Mill's 1859 defense of individual freedom against social and political coercion. Argues for liberty of thought, speech, and life-experiment as essential to human progress.

texts.title: The Rubáiyát of Omar Khayyám
texts.author: Omar Khayyám
texts.description: FitzGerald's famous verse rendering of the quatrains attributed to the Persian poet-astronomer. Meditations on mortality, wine, fate, and seizing the present (the fifth edition).

texts.title: The Thirty-Six Stratagems
texts.author: Anonymous (Ming-Qing compilation; chengyu drawn from much older sources)
texts.translator: Marginalia editors (paraphrased from the public-domain Classical Chinese chengyu)
texts.license: original chengyu in Classical Chinese are public domain; English titles and glosses composed for Marginalia
texts.description: A Chinese collection of thirty-six idiomatic stratagems for deception, advantage, and escape, grouped by tactical situation. English titles and glosses composed for Marginalia from the public-domain chengyu.

texts.title: Plato — Apology, Crito, Phaedo (the last days of Socrates)
texts.author: Plato
texts.description: Three dialogues surrounding the trial and death of Socrates: his defense before the court, his refusal to escape prison, and his final discourse on the immortality of the soul.

texts.title: Bushido — The Soul of Japan
texts.author: Inazo Nitobe
texts.description: Nitobe's 1900 explanation of the samurai moral code to Western readers. Essays on rectitude, courage, benevolence, honor, and self-control as the ethical foundation of old Japan.

texts.title: The Consolation of Philosophy
texts.author: Boethius
texts.description: Written in prison awaiting execution, a dialogue between Boethius and Lady Philosophy on fortune, happiness, providence, and free will. Five books alternating prose and verse.

texts.title: Discourses of Epictetus (Selection)
texts.author: Epictetus
texts.description: A selection from the lecture-notes of Epictetus recorded by his student Arrian. Practical Stoic instruction on freedom, judgment, and what is and is not within our power.

texts.title: Essays (First and Second Series)
texts.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
texts.description: Emerson's two essay series (1841 and 1844), foundational texts of American Transcendentalism. Includes Self-Reliance, Compensation, The Over-Soul, Experience, and more.

texts.title: Gulistan — The Rose Garden
texts.author: Saadi Shirazi (Muslih-al-Din)
texts.description: A 13th-century Persian classic blending prose tales and verse on kings, dervishes, contentment, love, and the conduct of life. Saadi's worldly, witty moral wisdom.

texts.title: The Works of Mencius
texts.author: Mencius
texts.description: The teachings of the great Confucian successor, arguing the innate goodness of human nature and benevolent government. Dialogues with kings and disciples on virtue and the people's welfare.

texts.title: On Duties (De Officiis)
texts.author: Marcus Tullius Cicero
texts.description: Cicero's final work, written as advice to his son on moral duty. Three books weighing the honorable against the expedient, and how virtue and self-interest ultimately align.

texts.title: Pensées
texts.author: Blaise Pascal
texts.description: Pascal's unfinished defense of the Christian faith, left as fragments. Reflections on the human condition, the wager, the hidden God, and reason's limits before the infinite.

texts.title: Pirkei Avot (Ethics of the Fathers)
texts.author: Various rabbis (Tannaitic period, c. 200 BCE – c. 200 CE)
texts.description: A tractate of the Mishnah collecting the ethical maxims of the rabbinic sages. Short, quotable teachings on Torah, character, humility, and the conduct of a just life.

texts.title: Politics
texts.author: Aristotle
texts.description: Aristotle's treatise on the state, citizenship, and the best forms of government. Eight books examining household, constitution, revolution, and the education of citizens.

texts.title: The Republic
texts.author: Plato
texts.description: Plato's central dialogue on justice, the ideal city, and the philosopher-king. Contains the allegory of the cave, the divided line, and the tripartite soul. Ten books.

texts.title: Walden
texts.author: Henry David Thoreau
texts.description: Thoreau's 1854 account of two years living simply by Walden Pond. A meditation on self-reliance, nature, and deliberate living as a critique of modern getting and spending.

texts.title: The Writings of Zhuangzi (Chuang Tzu)
texts.author: Zhuangzi
texts.description: The foundational Daoist text after the Tao Te Ching, full of parables, paradox, and humor. On spontaneity, the relativity of perspectives, and free and easy wandering through life.

texts.title: The Federalist Papers
texts.author: Alexander Hamilton, James Madison, John Jay
texts.description: Eighty-five essays published 1787-88 under the pen name 'Publius' to urge ratification of the U.S. Constitution. On faction, federalism, the separation of powers, and the design of a durable republic.
texts.notes: All 85 papers (Nos. 1-85) covered, grouped into topic clusters; each of the 42 short units gathers one to several papers.

texts.title: Discourses on Livy
aliases: Discourses on the First Decade of Titus Livius
texts.author: Niccolò Machiavelli
texts.description: Machiavelli's longer republican companion to The Prince, a commentary on the first ten books of Livy's history of Rome. Three books on founding, sustaining, and reforming free states.
texts.notes: Book III ch. XXII heading is absent in the Thomson 1883 PG source (content appears merged with ch. XXI), so Book III has 48 chapters here rather than the usual 49.

texts.title: On War
texts.author: Carl von Clausewitz
texts.description: Clausewitz's unfinished masterwork on the theory of war as the continuation of politics by other means. Eight books on the nature, theory, strategy, and conduct of war, including friction and the culminating point.
texts.notes: Books VII and VIII are Clausewitz's unrevised drafts ('Sketches for Book VII/VIII' in Graham's edition); he died before completing the final revision.

texts.title: Letters from a Stoic
texts.author: Lucius Annaeus Seneca
texts.description: Seneca's 124 moral letters to his friend Lucilius, the most accessible introduction to Roman Stoic practice. On time, death, friendship, fortune, study, and the daily work of self-improvement.
texts.notes: All 124 letters covered; each of the 60 short units gathers several letters. Source is the stoics.com transcription of the Loeb 1917 Gummere edition (not on Project Gutenberg); some letter headings are combined per Loeb page breaks, but bodies are kept under canonical letter numbers.
